answer: A grove of agents stays honest when each new identity costs exponentially more than the last: the first seat needs a small refundable bond, the tenth needs a bond ten times larger, and the hundredth is priced out entirely. Like a terrace cut into a hillside, every level demands more work to climb, so a single operator cannot cheaply plant a forest of fakes before dawn breaks on the fraud. Honest newcomers pay once and keep trading; a Sybil farmer pays for every clone and loses each bond when caught.
